title: The Spanish Civil War (1936–1939)
summary: The long- and short-term causes of the Spanish Civil War, why foreign intervention mattered, why Franco's Nationalists won and what followed.

keyterms.definition: Spanish republic proclaimed in April 1931 after King Alfonso XIII left Spain.
Right-wing Catholic coalition led by José María Gil-Robles, largest party after the November 1933 election.
Left-wing electoral alliance that won the February 1936 election.
Rebel side in the civil war led by army generals, eventually under Francisco Franco, backed by the Church, monarchists and the Falange.
Side defending the elected government: liberals, socialists, communists, anarchists and Basque and Catalan nationalists.
Body set up in London in 1936 by Britain and France to prevent foreign involvement; Germany, Italy and the USSR ignored it.
German air and ground force that fought for Franco and bombed Guernica in April 1937.
Foreign volunteers, organised by the Comintern, who fought for the Republic.
Spanish fascist party, merged by Franco in 1937 into a single movement under his control.

questions.prompt: Which reform programme of the Republic's first government (1931–33) angered the right?
options: Army reform, land reform and limits on the Catholic Church
questions.explanation: Azaña's reforms alienated officers, landowners and Catholics, while disappointing the left for being too slow.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: April 1931, November 1933, October 1934, February 1936, July 1936.

questions.statement: General Franco helped suppress the Asturias miners' rising in 1934.
questions.explanation: Moroccan troops and the Foreign Legion were used; the brutal repression deepened polarisation.

questions.text: The left-wing alliance that won the February 1936 election was the ___ Front.
questions.explanation: Its victory was followed by land seizures, strikes and political violence that conspirators used to justify a coup.

questions.prompt: Which event in July 1936 was used as the immediate justification for the military uprising?
options: The murder of monarchist leader José Calvo Sotelo
questions.explanation: The killing by government police on 13 July 1936 hastened a coup already being planned by General Mola.

questions.prompt: Match each long-term cause to its description.

pairs.right: Huge estates and landless labourers in the south
Clash between Catholic tradition and anticlericalism
Officers with a tradition of intervening in politics
Catalan and Basque demands for autonomy

questions.explanation: Historians such as Paul Preston stress these deep divisions behind the 1936 crisis.

questions.statement: The July 1936 coup succeeded across all of Spain within a few days.
questions.explanation: It failed in Madrid, Barcelona and much of the industrial north and east, turning a coup into a civil war.

questions.prompt: How did Franco's Army of Africa reach mainland Spain in summer 1936?
options: It was airlifted with help from German and Italian aircraft
questions.explanation: This early foreign help was crucial, since the navy largely stayed loyal to the Republic.

questions.text: The CEDA was led by José María ___.
questions.explanation: CEDA's entry into government in October 1934 triggered the Asturias rising.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the Republican side?
options: A divided coalition of liberals, socialists, communists and anarchists
A single communist party controlled by Moscow from the start
questions.explanation: These divisions, such as the May Days in Barcelona (1937), weakened the Republic's war effort.

questions.prompt: Why did Britain and France promote non-intervention?
options: Fear of a wider European war and, in Britain, suspicion of the Republic's left
They had signed a treaty with the USSR
questions.explanation: Non-intervention denied the Republic legal arms purchases while Germany and Italy continued to aid Franco.

questions.text: The German ___ Legion bombed the Basque town of Guernica in April 1937.
questions.explanation: The raid on market day became a symbol of modern terror bombing, painted by Picasso.

questions.prompt: Match each foreign power to its role.

pairs.right: Air power and advisers for Franco
Tens of thousands of troops for Franco
Arms for the Republic, paid with Spanish gold

questions.explanation: Foreign intervention turned Spain into a rehearsal for wider war.

questions.statement: The International Brigades were volunteers who fought for the Nationalists.
questions.explanation: They fought for the Republic; about 35,000 volunteers from many countries served, recruited through the Comintern.

questions.prompt: Which was a key reason for Nationalist victory?
options: Unified command under Franco and more reliable foreign aid
Control of all major cities from the start
questions.explanation: Franco merged rival right-wing groups in 1937, while Republicans quarrelled and their Soviet aid declined.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: November 1936, April 1937, May 1937, July–November 1938, March 1939.

questions.text: Franco, made head of the Nationalist state in October 1936, was known by the title ___, meaning leader.
questions.explanation: In April 1937 he also merged the Falange and Carlists into one party (FET y de las JONS), giving the Nationalists political unity.

questions.prompt: What happened in Spain after the war ended on 1 April 1939?
options: Mass repression: tens of thousands executed and many imprisoned or exiled
Spain joined the Axis in war immediately
questions.explanation: Franco ruled as dictator until 1975; Spain stayed officially non-belligerent in the Second World War.

questions.statement: Germany used Spain to test weapons and tactics later used in the Second World War.
questions.explanation: Dive-bombing and combined air–ground tactics were developed with the Condor Legion.

questions.prompt: How did the Spanish Civil War affect international relations?
options: It drew Germany and Italy closer and exposed the weakness of Anglo-French policy
questions.explanation: Cooperation in Spain helped form the Rome–Berlin Axis (1936) and convinced Stalin the West would not stand up to fascism.
